result.question: What does the old prophet do after hearing men?

readings.answer: He instructs his sons to saddle the donkey for him.
readings.support: Then the old prophet instructed his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.”

readings.answer: He goes and finds the body lying in the road.
readings.support: and he went and found the body lying in the road

readings.answer: He lifts up the body, lays it on the donkey, and brings it back to his city to mourn and bury him.
readings.support: So the old prophet lifted up the body of the man of God, laid it on the donkey, and brought it back to his own city to mourn for him and bury him.

assessments.reason: The passage says, “Then the old prophet instructed his sons, ‘Saddle the donkey for me,’” which matches the first part of the key, though it omits the second action.
The text states, “and he went and found the body lying in the road,” matching the key’s second action even though it doesn’t mention the saddling.

“So the old prophet lifted up the body… and brought it back… to mourn for him and bury him” is supported by the window as an action after hearing, but it goes beyond the key’s specified steps rather than contradicting them.
